mekanisme-perdagangan.title: Trading Mechanism
mekanisme-perdagangan.intro: A quick overview of the core futures trading flow: selecting an instrument, placing orders, and managing risk through margin, leverage, and position management.

sections.title: General Flow
bullets: Pick an instrument that matches your risk profile and goals.
Choose a direction (buy/long or sell/short).
Define contract/lot size and your entry–exit plan.
Place an order (market/limit/stop) via the trading platform.
Monitor positions, margin, and market conditions; adjust when needed.

sections.title: Margin & Leverage
paragraphs: Margin is the collateral used to open a position. Leverage provides larger exposure relative to deposited funds, which can amplify both profits and losses.
bullets: Understand initial margin and maintenance margin requirements.
Avoid excessive leverage; align it with your tolerance.
Use stop loss and take profit to control risk.

sections.title: Risk Management
bullets: Use disciplined position sizing.
Diversify and avoid concentrating on a single instrument.
Watch high-impact news releases (e.g., rates, inflation, NFP).
Review performance regularly (trading journal).

simbol-indeks.title: Index Symbols
simbol-indeks.intro: Symbols (codes) uniquely identify instruments in a trading system. Understanding symbols helps you ensure you trade the correct product (e.g., equity index, FX, or commodities).

sections.title: Example Index Symbols
bullets: HKK50_BBJ / HKK5U_BBJ: contracts based on a Hong Kong index (Hang Seng).
JPK50_BBJ / JPK5U_BBJ: contracts based on a Japanese index (Nikkei).

sections.title: How to Read the Code
bullets: The prefix often indicates the underlying (e.g., HKK50, JPK50).
A suffix such as _BBJ can be an internal/product identifier in the system.
Number/letter variants can represent contract size or contract series.

sections.title: Tips
bullets: Always check contract specs: point value, spread/fees, and trading hours.
Make sure the symbol matches your account/product type.

loco-london-gold.title: Loco London Gold
loco-london-gold.intro: Loco London Gold refers to gold transactions settled in London. International spot gold prices often reference this standard and are commonly quoted as XAU/USD.

sections.title: What Does It Mean?
bullets: “Loco London” refers to settlement in the London bullion market.
Typically associated with good-delivery bars within London clearing.
Widely used as a global benchmark for spot gold.

sections.title: Key Price Drivers
bullets: USD strength and interest-rate policy (the Fed).
Inflation and inflation expectations.
Risk sentiment (risk-on/risk-off) and geopolitics.
Physical demand, ETFs, and central bank reserves.

sections.title: Risk Notes
bullets: Gold can be highly volatile during major economic releases.
Manage leverage and apply proper risk controls.

summer-winter.title: Summer & Winter
summer-winter.intro: During certain periods, trading hours may shift due to Daylight Saving Time (DST) in some countries. This is commonly referred to as “summer time” and “winter time”.

sections.title: Why Do Hours Change?
bullets: When DST is active (summer time), local clocks move forward by 1 hour.
When DST ends (winter time), hours return to normal.
This can make global market sessions appear shifted relative to your local time.

sections.title: Impact on Trading
bullets: Session changes may shift typical volatility windows.
Economic release schedules follow local time; adjust accordingly.
Update alerts, analysis routines, and execution plans.

sections.title: Practical Tips
bullets: Check the latest economic calendar and market hours at the start of the week.
Set reminders for DST transition periods (often March/November).
